name: HydraSession
concept: An autonomous session/auth-confusion toolkit for allowlisted lab web apps that crawls endpoints, harvests cookies/JWTs/role parameters from responses and page JS, and feeds them to a token mutation engine (JWT alg confusion, none-alg, unsigned-token rebasing, HMAC secret brute, cookie/param tampering, predictable-session analysis) that replays mutants and auto-escalates to admin via an IDOR + role-parameter traversal loop. It maps the app's authorization surface, then iterates harvest-mutate-replay-escalate until an admin-authenticated state is reached in the lab.
attack_vectors: JWT alg confusion: none/case-variant forging and RS256-to-HS256 rebase using discovered public keys
Weak HMAC session secret recovery via offline wordlist/short-key brute, then full token forgery
Token replay & misuse: cross-endpoint replay, privilege rebinding, timestamp/expiry stretching
Cookie tampering: signed-cookie signature stripping, role/flag bit-flip, predictable session-ID inference
IDOR: object-ID traversal to harvest admin tokens
Role-parameter tampering: isAdmin/groups[]/permission-claim mutation and privilege re-request
novelty_angle: Off-the-shelf tools stop at single-stage attacks (a JWT cracker, cookie scanner, IDOR fuzzer). This treats the whole auth/session lifecycle as one autonomous loop: live schema inference on harvested tokens drives a prioritized mutation engine, and an escalation brain picks the highest-credibility mutant to replay — mimicking an attacker who reads the app's own auth grammar before striking.
dependencies: Python 3 stdlib (http.server, urllib, base64, hmac, hashlib)
requests or stdlib urllib for HTTP
optional PyJWT; pure-stdlib JWT parser otherwise
small bundled session-secret wordlist for HMAC brute
scope_gate: Single allowlist object (config file or --lab-cidr plus implicit 127.0.0.0/8,10/8,172.16/12,192.168/16): every fetch, replay, mutation, escalation resolves final host and is refused if outside allowlist. WARN banner on first run; public-range host aborts before any network I/O.
